text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Aug 13 edition of several Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Grain crops in Russia this year are expected to be about 80 million tonnes which is higher than in 1996 and 1995, says Russia's agriculture minister.
- Tatarstan is planning to issue Eurobonds in November.
- Russia's 1998 budget presupposes tightening government control over the way the regions spend federal budget money.
- Grain crops in Russia this year are expected to be higher than last year and grain prices may fall, experts say.
- The government can no longer afford numerous social benefits to servicemen, the government paper says.

- President Boris Yeltsin, apparently alarmed by the possibility of a rise of separatist feelings among Cossacks, has suspended a decree on Cossacks' state service adopted by the local authorities of Krasnodar in southern Russia.
- Rouble re-denomination will not harm ordinary Russians, says the Central Bank's first deputy chairman Alexander Khandruyev.
